To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) people from East Asian cultures tend to prefer and perform better with holistic Web sites, while people from Western cultures tend to prefer analytic Web sites; (b) people from East and West cultures are more likely to use and perform better with Web sites that are designed according to their own cultural cognitive style; and (c) Web site designers can improve usability by accommodating culturally diverse user groups.
holistic cognitive style users prefer Web sites with more holistic cognitive style design, while analytic cognitive style users prefer sites with more analytic cognitive style design.
the cognitive style of a Web site designer influences his or her information design and organization of Web pages, and this influence is mediated by culture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of cognitive style on Web design and the impact of Web design on user preferences and performance.
how cultural cognitive styles influence Web site design.
the influence of cultural cognitive styles on online information design, and how this can be used to improve computer-mediated communications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cultural cognitive style of a designer influences his/her design decisions, and these design decisions influence user preferences and performance.
holistic cognitive styles are associated with a preference for holistic information design, while analytic cognitive styles are associated to a preference for analytic information design.
cultural cognitive styles influence the design of Web sites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cultural cognitive styles have a significant influence on the design of online information.

the cultural cognitive design theory provides a framework for the development of Web sites that accommodate the cognitive styles of users from diverse cultural backgrounds, thus enhancing the usability and user satisfaction of Web sites.
culture influences cognitive styles, which in turn influences online information design.
The main takeaway from our work is that
designers should be aware of the influence of cultural cognitive styles in designing Web sites.
cultural cognitive style differences are important to consider when designing Web sites for global audiences.
designers need to be aware of how cultural cognitive styles affect their design and how these designs affect the user's cognitive processes.
